Fort Mckavett, moving southeast at 25 mph.

properties.description:

for patchy dense freezing fog near the larger rivers and lakes. This
could lead to slick spots on area roads, particularly bridges and

venture out this morning.

properties.description:

rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Del Norte County in northwestern California...

* WHEN...Until 445 AM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 137 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
SMWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 400 AM CST.

* At 257 AM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 44 NM south of Port Oconnor, moving east at
10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from
20 to 60 NM.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 15 at 12:29AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at
favored breakpoints. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking
waves of 20 to 25 ft, with occasional sets of 25 to 35 ft at
favored breakpoints.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST today. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM today through 4 AM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.
Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 15 at 2:27AM CST until November 17 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
3 to 8 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip
Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this evening
to 6 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this
evening through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide
at 1115 PM tonight and again at 1122 PM Monday night.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 9:08PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 22 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 8:26PM PST until November 15 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an
exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal
structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

feet lowering to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous
rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to
moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to
significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is
unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-
northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into
next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely
peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to
moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially
when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these
impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.
properties.instruction:

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 14 at 5:04PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Moderate snow and winds are expected in the Eastern Brooks Range
through Saturday night. Total snow accumulations could range
between 2 and 5 inches during this time. Wind gusts to 35 mph
could produce areas of blowing and drifting snow. Travel may
become difficult throughout this period.

NWSheadline: Blowing Snow with Moderate Accumulations Expected in the Eastern Brooks Range

properties.areaDesc: Upper Tanana Valley; Delta Junction; Tanana Flats; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area; Nenana
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 14 at 5:04PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Patchy freezing fog is possible through much of the night for an
area stretching northwestward from Tok to Nenana, including the
Fairbanks Metro Area, which may cause a light slippery glaze to
form on surfaces. Use extra caution if you must travel through
the night.

properties.areaDesc: Maui County Windward Waters; Big Island Windward Waters
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 14 at 3:08PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A moderate, long-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees will
build across Hawaiian waters on Sunday and peak late Sunday and
Monday as the period shortens to 13 seconds. The swell will
produce moderate to heavy surges in north-facing harbors,
especially at Kahului and Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these
harbors should exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels
and when entering or leaving port. The swell will diminish
Tuesday.

NWSheadline: SURGES AT KAHULUI AND HILO HARBORS SUNDAY AND MONDAY

properties.areaDesc: McMullen, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:02PM CST until November 17 at 12:24AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CST Saturday the stage was 13.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 14.9 feet Sunday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage Monday.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FROM THIS EVENING TO LATE MONDAY NIGHT

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:51PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. River levels are
expected to remain steady into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on
Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water
covers Mullet Lake Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:49PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue remain steady with slight deviations in
river levels through at least early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Saturday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Saturday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.1 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:47PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast early next week due to a combination of northerly
winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream heavy
rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 4:26PM PST until November 16 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along
the coast. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large
breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 10 AM PST Sunday. For
the High Surf Warning, from 10 AM Sunday to 10 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from recent high surf events will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

possible.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* WHEN...From late Monday night through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

morning as a strong low pressure system moves through the Bering.
Winds will gradually lighten but remain gusty through Wednesday.

event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.

into Monday morning. Waves and surf remain hazardous Monday, but
gradually diminish through Monday evening.

hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves
will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas.

Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday.

and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

flow peaking at 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream  also indicated a stage of 9.93 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
